_comment: Canonical (percent_left, pace_delta) -> signal level truth table.
Read by BOTH halves of the codebase so the Swift and Python ramps cannot
It lives inside the SwiftPM test target because SwiftPM resources cannot
reference files outside the target directory (same constraint that put
golden-v2-snapshot.json here). Python reads it by relative path.
This file is the interim stand-in for a single shared implementation --
see the [future] centralization row in TASKS.md. Until that lands, a
change to one surface's ramp that is not mirrored on the other fails
here, on both sides, rather than shipping as a rendering inconsistency.
`nan` is spelled as the string "nan" because JSON has no non-finite
literal; both readers translate it to their language's NaN.

cases.why: No percentage at all -- nothing to color.
Non-finite percentage fails percentIsValid.
Above 100 violates INV-3; refuse to color rather than guess. Note the pre-2026-08-05 percent ramp returned green here.
Below 0 violates INV-3; same refusal as above.
Depleted. Red regardless of pace -- there is nothing left to pace.
Rounds to zero, so percentIsDepleted is true (matches snapshot.py).
Depletion outranks a healthy pace: exhausted is exhausted.
Rounds to 1, so not depleted -- but the pace branch lands in red anyway.
Just under the 0.5 depletion ceiling: depleted, and depletion outranks a healthy pace.

Exactly at the ceiling and therefore NOT depleted, so pace decides and this is on pace. This pair is the regression test for the rounding divergence: Python's banker's round(0.5) == 0 made this red on the TUI while Swift's (0.5).rounded() == 1 made it green on Mac/iOS. Both now compare against a 0.5 bound instead of rounding, so no rounding mode is involved.
No pace data: fall back to the legacy percent ramp rather than lose color.
Fallback ramp boundary, inclusive (unchanged from the percent-only ramp).
Fallback ramp, just below the green boundary.
Fallback ramp boundary, inclusive.
Fallback ramp, just below the yellow boundary.
Fallback ramp boundary, inclusive.
Fallback ramp, just below the orange boundary. NOTE: this is one of the two cases where 'orange or worse' does NOT equal windowWarns -- with no pace there is nothing to warn on.
Non-finite pace is treated as absent: fall back to the percent ramp.
1% left 5 minutes before a 5-hour reset. Essentially on pace, so NOT red -- the case that motivated the pace ramp.
50% left 5 minutes before reset: a non-event. The percent ramp called this yellow.
20% left with 80% of the window still to run: the genuinely alarming case. The percent ramp called this orange.
Ahead of pace. The percent ramp called this orange.
Exactly on pace is healthy -- the green boundary is inclusive.
Exactly -0.10 does NOT warn (windowWarns is strictly <), so it must not reach orange.
First value that warns. Anchors 'orange or worse' to windowWarns in snapshot.py and WarningPredicate.swift.
Orange/red boundary, inclusive.
Burning down more than 25 points faster than the clock.
